title: I Took a Night Job at a Lake Campground. There Was One Rule. #shorts #scarystories
description:
Count the tents at midnight. There are always twelve.

Follow for a new scary story every night.

#scarystory #horrorstories #creepy #shorts

beats.text: Last summer, I took a night job watching over Pine Lake Campground.
The owner gave me a little cabin by the water. And one rule.
He made me save it on my phone.
The first few weeks were quiet. Families. Campfires. Kids roasting marshmallows.
Every night at midnight, I walked the shore and counted. Twelve tents. Always twelve.
Then came the last night of August. Almost everyone had gone home.
Only one family was left. But when I counted, I got thirteen.
The new tent stood right at the edge of the water. No car. No fire. No footprints.
My phone buzzed. It was the owner.
I told him thirteen, and asked if I should check on it.
His answer came instantly.

overlay.message: NO. Lock your door. Don't open it for anyone until sunrise.

beats.text: So I locked myself in the cabin, sat by the door, and waited.
At two in the morning, someone knocked. Three slow knocks.
Then a little girl's voice said, please let me in. I can't find my mom.
I looked out the window. A small figure stood on the dock, soaking wet.
She knocked until dawn. I didn't open the door. I didn't sleep.
At sunrise, the thirteenth tent was gone. So was the last family.
Three days later, I saw their faces on the news.
I quit that morning, and drove away without looking back.
A week later, the owner sent me one last message.

overlay.message: Thank you for keeping the door shut. The guard before you opened it.

beats.text: I never found out what happened to that guard.
But this summer, Pine Lake is hiring again. And they're looking for two.
